chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh, may Allah have mercy upon him, narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Ja'far al-Dawaniqi said to him in al-Hira during the days of Abu al-Abbas: 'O Abu Abdillah, what is the matter with a man from your Shia who extracts what is in his chest in one session so that his creed is recognized?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is due to the sweetness of faith in their chests; from its sweetness, they reveal it openly.'
ai.seo_question: Why do Shia Muslims openly reveal their beliefs according to the hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Sifat al-Shia*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) attributes the Shia’s public disclosure of their beliefs (al-tubdī) not to political necessity, but to the profound spiritual comfort (ḥalāwat al-īmān) that fills their hearts. This internal sweetness renders the fear of concealment (al-ṭaqiyya) unnecessary, allowing them to manifest their creed openly as a natural expression of their faith. This concept highlights the Shia theological view that sincerity of heart naturally leads to transparency in belief, distinguishing them from those who hide their faith due to anxiety or insincerity.

en.badr-shahin: Mohammad bin Ali Majilwayh, Allah may have mercy upon him, …

In al-Hira during the reign of Abu al-Abbas, Abu Ja’far ad-Dawaniqi said to Imam Abu Abdullah (a) “O Abu Abdullah, I noticed that any individual of the Shia speak out all that he hides in one session so that his trend would be easily known. Why is that?” The Imam (a) answered: This is because of the sweetness of faith that the Shia carry in their chests. For that sweetness, they show the hidden all at once.
